questions.q: What is the key difference between plain Secure Data Sharing and the Native App Framework?
options: Secure Data Sharing shares only data; the Native App Framework also packages and ships application logic (Snowpark code, Streamlit apps, stored procedures) that runs inside the consumer's account
Native Apps can only be used by the same account that created them
There is no real difference -- they are the same feature with two names
Secure Data Sharing requires copying data between accounts; Native Apps never share anything at all
questions.explain: Secure Data Sharing shares the data itself. The Native App Framework builds on that same mechanism but adds real application logic a consumer can install and run.

questions.q: What two pieces does Snowflake's documentation say matter most inside an application package?
options: A CSV export and a README
The manifest file and the setup script
A Dockerfile and a requirements.txt
A warehouse definition and a database schema only
questions.explain: The manifest file defines the app's configuration and setup properties; the setup script is the SQL that actually creates the app's objects when installed.

questions.q: When does the setup script actually run?
options: Automatically, whenever a consumer installs or upgrades the app (or the provider installs it for testing)
Every time any query runs inside the consumer's account
Manually, triggered by the consumer typing a special command each time they use the app
Only once, when the provider first writes the code, never again
questions.explain: The setup script runs on install or upgrade, creating the app's objects inside whichever account is installing it -- consumer or provider (during testing).

questions.q: Where does a consumer's own data live while a Native App's logic runs against it?
options: It stays inside the consumer's own account the entire time -- the provider's logic runs there without the provider needing standing access to see the data directly
It's automatically copied to the provider's account for processing
It's temporarily uploaded to the Snowflake Marketplace
The consumer must manually export and re-import their data for the app to work
questions.explain: The framework is built specifically so application logic runs inside the consumer's own account against their own data, without the provider needing direct access to it.

questions.q: What does the Snowflake Marketplace add that a private listing alone does not?
options: Public discoverability -- any Snowflake customer can find and install the app without a maintained one-to-one sharing relationship, and listings can be free or paid
Only Marketplace listings can include a setup script
Private listings cannot include application logic, only data
Marketplace listings are always free and cannot be monetized
questions.explain: A private listing targets specific named accounts, the same as data sharing. The Marketplace opens public discovery and is the real monetization path, since listings can be paid.
